metric_rationale: By isolating trials where Tallying encounters a tie (i.e., both options win on an equal number of features), we can cleanly separate the two theories. Tallying predicts random guessing (0.5) on these trials regardless of its parameters. In contrast, WADD uses the specific validities to break the tie, consistently favoring the option with higher validity-weighted features. Measuring the proportion of choices that align with WADD's prediction on these specific tie trials yields exactly 0.5 for Tallying and strictly > 0.5 for WADD.

The metric contrasts the probability of choosing option B on two specific trial types where Tallying and WADD systematically diverge. On both Trial 4 and Trial 9, each option has exactly one unique winning feature, so Tallying always registers a tie and predicts a 50/50 choice (difference = 0). However, WADD weighs features by their validities. In Trial 4, B's unique advantage (0.78) outweighs A's (0.55), leading WADD to favor B. In Trial 9, A's unique advantage (0.95) heavily outweighs B's (0.55), leading WADD to favor A. Thus, WADD predicts a positive difference (P(B|Trial 4) - P(B|Trial 9) > 0), whereas Tallying predicts exactly zero.

This metric calculates the proportion of choices that exactly align with the Take-The-Best (TTB) heuristic's predictions. TTB strictly follows the validity order of features (0, 2, 1, 3). WADD, on the other hand, allows for subjective weighting of validities (via the `weights` parameter) and compensatory evaluation, meaning it will frequently deviate from the rigid lexicographic choice pattern of TTB. Thus, data simulated under TTB will have a much higher TTB-match proportion than data simulated under WADD.

Trial 11 is specifically designed to pit a single higher-validity cue against multiple lower-validity cues. TTB will predictably choose the option with the single higher-validity cue (feature 1, validity 0.84), while WADD's compensatory nature allows the combined weight of the two lower-validity cues (validities 0.64 and 0.55) to outvote it. By computing the proportion of choices that align with the TTB prediction on this specific trial, we obtain a metric that is high for TTB and low for WADD, cleanly discriminating the two theories.
